facts.text: Vermillion Township was named for the Vermillion River, whose Dakota name translates to the river's current name.
Vermillion's early growth surged when the Hastings and Dakota Railroad arrived in 1866, opening the area to farmers.
The Vermillion River meanders through the town, shaping its landscape and providing a natural corridor for wildlife.
Vermillion’s valley shapes local topography, creating narrow floodplains, wetlands, and upland prairies that transition into riparian zones along the riverbanks.
Vermillion preserves its historic Main Street and rural charm, keeping the town a peaceful suburb amid Minnesota’s fastest-growing counties.
Below the Mississippi bottomland, the Vermillion River splits into two streams that form the Vermillion Slough.
